title: Vaginal homeostasis features of Vulvovaginal Candidiasis through vaginal metabolic profiling.
authors: Chen, Xinyi; Wang, Jinbo; Chen, Jing; Wang, Guanghua; Zhang, Runjie; Qiu, Jin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过代谢组学分析外阴阴道念珠菌病的阴道代谢特征，并做分子对接，但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，与课题无关。
abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is an inflammatory disease primarily infected by Candida albicans. The condition has good short-term treatment effects, high recurrence, and seriously affects the quality of life of women. Metabolomics has been applied to research a variety of inflammatory diseases. In the present study, the vaginal metabolic profiles of VVC patients and healthy populations (Cnotrol (CTL)) were explored by a non-targeted metabolomics approach. In total, 211 differential metabolites were identified, with the VVC group having 128 over-expressed and 83 under-expressed metabolites compared with healthy individuals. Functional analysis showed that these metabolites were mainly involved in amino acid metabolism and lipid metabolism. In addition, network software analysis indicated that the differential metabolites were associated with mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling and NF-kappaB signaling. Further molecular docking suggested that linoleic acid can bind to the acyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSL1) protein, which has been shown to be associated with multiple inflammatory diseases and is an upstream regulator of the MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways that mediate inflammation. Therefore, our preliminary analysis results suggest that VVC has a unique metabolic profile. Linoleic acid, a significantly elevated unsaturated fatty acid in the VVC group, may promote VVC development through the ACSL1/MAPK and ACSL1/NF-kappaB signaling pathways. This study's findings contribute to further exploring the mechanism of VVC infection and providing new perspectives for the treatment of Candida albicans vaginal infection.
abstract_zh: 外阴阴道念珠菌病（VVC）是一种主要由白色念珠菌（Candida albicans）感染引起的炎症性疾病。该病短期治疗效果良好，但复发率高，严重影响女性生活质量。代谢组学已应用于多种炎症性疾病的研究。本研究采用非靶向代谢组学方法，探讨了VVC患者与健康人群（对照组（CTL））的阴道代谢谱。共鉴定出211种差异代谢物，其中VVC组与健康个体相比，有128种代谢物表达上调，83种表达下调。功能分析显示，这些代谢物主要涉及氨基酸代谢和脂质代谢。此外，网络软件分析表明，差异代谢物与丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）信号通路和NF-κB信号通路相关。进一步的分子对接提示，亚油酸可与酰基辅酶A合成酶1（ACSL1）蛋白结合，该蛋白已被证明与多种炎症性疾病相关，并且是介导炎症的MAPK和NF-κB信号通路的上游调节因子。因此，我们的初步分析结果表明，VVC具有独特的代谢谱。亚油酸是VVC组中显著升高的不饱和脂肪酸，可能通过ACSL1/MAPK和ACSL1/NF-κB信号通路促进VVC的发展。本研究的发现有助于进一步探索VVC感染的机制，并为治疗白色念珠菌阴道感染提供新的视角。
